source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: And Yeshua the Anointed One [Messiah] summoned the twelve of his disciples and gave to them authority [or: capability] and power over all the demonic spirits [or: harmful forces] and to bring healing to the afflicted [or: diseased]

translation_notes: קרא (QR'): Candidates: H7121 'to call out/summon', H7122 'to encounter', H7124 'partridge'. Context is summoning disciples, so H7121 'called/summoned' fits perfectly.
משיח (MSHYCH): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder/utter', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'shrub'. Following the proper name Yeshua, this is clearly a title — H4899 'Anointed One'.
עשר ('SR): Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6240 '-teen (in combination)'. Preceded by 'the two' (ה2נים), this forms 'twelve' — H6240 is the combining form.
ה2נים: The 2 likely represents שנ (two), reading השנים — 'the two'. Combined with עשר = twelve.
ה2דים: The 2 likely represents שד (demon), reading השדים — 'the demons'. Context of power over spiritual forces and healing supports this.
textual_notes: ה2נים and ה2דים use a numeral abbreviation (2) whose expansion is inferred from context. ה2נים likely = השנים (the two), and ה2דים likely = השדים (the demons). The use of '2' as an abbreviation for שנ/שד is unusual and could theoretically represent other words.
יכול״ת (with abbreviation marks) appears to be יכולת 'ability/capability' — a noun form from the root יכל. This is not a standard Strong's entry but is well-attested in later Hebrew.

verses.literal: And Yeshua [the] Anointed called the twelve [of] his disciples and gave to them ability and power over all the demons and to heal the sick

verses.translation: And he sent them forth to proclaim [or: seek out, inquire into] the kingdom [or: dominion, reign] of the LORD

translation_notes: ושלחם: Root שלח 'to send' with vav-consecutive and 3ms suffix on the object (them). The candidate לחם (H3898 'to fight', H3899 'bread') shares some consonants but the leading ו+ש clearly marks this as ושלחם from שלח 'and he sent them'.
מלכות: Candidates: H4438 'kingdom/dominion', H3575 'Cuth/Cuthah'. In context of preaching a divine reign, H4438 is the natural reading.
textual_notes: לדרוש: Root דרש 'to seek, inquire, expound'. No Strong's candidates were provided but the root is unambiguous — H1875. The infinitive construct with ל prefix means 'to seek/proclaim'.

verses.literal: And he sent them to seek [the] kingdom of YHWH

verses.translation: And he said to them: Do not carry [any] thing in [your] hand — not a staff, not bread, not money [lit: stone], not coins. And [the] father and mother of the girl — to the girl there [old/existing] — in his saying... she called, she was called, she went out, she had gone out

translation_notes: ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. With vav-consecutive and context of giving instructions, H559 'and he said' is clear.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. After 'you shall not carry' — an object is expected, so H1697 'a thing' fits.

מעות: The consonants מעות could derive from עות (H5790 'to hasten', H5791 'to wrest') but in context of items not to carry, this is the well-known post-biblical Hebrew word for 'coins/money' (from the root מעה). No exact Strong's match; closest contextual meaning is 'money/coins'.
ואם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Following ואב 'and father', H517 'and mother' creates the natural pair.
הנערה: Candidates: H5291 'a girl', H5292 'Naarah (proper name)'. Context suggests a narrative about a girl, H5291.
ישנה: H3466 'Jeshanah' (a place). But the consonants also support ישנה from ישן 'old/existing/sleeping'. Context is unclear; possibly 'there is [already there]' or 'sleeping'.
textual_notes: This section appears to contain two distinct passages merged or a textual corruption. The first part (instructions about not carrying items) is coherent. The second part beginning with 'and father and mother the girl...' followed by fragmentary elements (ה ־ ה תה ־ א) and repeated verb forms (קראה/קראתה, יצאה/יצאתה) is extremely difficult. The repeated pairs of verb forms (3fs perfect with and without ה suffix) suggest a grammatical paradigm or gloss rather than narrative text.

ל״ח״ם and א״ב״ן use abbreviation marks (geresh/double-geresh) suggesting these are treated as abbreviations or marked words. ל״ח״ם = לחם 'bread' (H3899), א״ב״ן = אבן 'stone' — in context 'stone' likely means money/coins (as small stones were used as weights/currency markers).
The fragment ה ־ ה תה ־ א is extremely obscure. It may represent a damaged portion, a marginal notation, or abbreviations. No confident translation is possible for this fragment.

The section from ואב onward may be a different text entirely (possibly a narrative about a girl being called/going out, perhaps related to the raising of Jairus's daughter or another account). The verb paradigm pairs (קראה/קראתה and יצאה/יצאתה) could be scribal notes showing alternative conjugation forms.

verses.literal: And he said to them not you shall carry a thing in hand not a staff not bread not a stone not money and father and mother the girl to the girl there is in his saying ... she called she was called she went out she had gone out

verses.translation: And into whatever house you enter, there you shall stay, and from there you shall not go out.

translation_notes: ובאי: Candidates include H335 'where?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. With the prefix ו + ב, and followed by זה בית, the reading 'and in which(ever)' using H335 ('where? / which?') produces the coherent instruction: 'and in whichever house you enter'.
זה: H2088 'this/that' vs H2089 'a sheep' vs H2090 'this/that'. As a demonstrative modifying בית, H2088 is the clear choice.
בית: H1004 'house' vs H1006 'Bajith (place)' vs H3487 'object marker'. As the object entered and dwelt in, 'house' is obvious.
שם: H8033 'there' vs H8034 'name' vs H8035 'Shem' vs H8036 'name'. Following 'that you enter' and preceding 'you shall remain', 'there' (H8033) is the coherent adverb.
textual_notes: ומ<ם contains a damaged character (marked '<'). The likely reading is ומשם 'and from there'.

verses.literal: And in whichever house that you enter there you shall remain and from there not you shall go out

verses.translation: And [as for] those who do not receive you, go out from that city and shake off [or: remove] the dust of your feet as a testimony against them.

translation_notes: העיר: Candidates H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young donkey'. After 'go out from that the ___', 'city' is the only coherent reading — one exits a city, not a donkey or angel.
ועפר: Candidates H6080 'to be dust', H6081 'Epher (name)', H6082 'fawn', H6083 'dust/earth'. Before 'your feet', 'dust' (H6083) produces the coherent image of shaking dust off one's feet.
לעדות: H5715 'testimony'. With ל- prefix = 'for testimony'. Straightforward.

verses.literal: And those who not receive you you shall go out from that the city and dust [of] your feet you shall remove for testimony against them

verses.translation: And when you go out from there, go through [or: search out] the houses, preaching [or: seeking] and healing the sick in every place.

translation_notes: בכל: H3605 'the whole / all / every' vs H3606 (Aramaic equivalent). Hebrew context favors H3605.
מקום: H4725 'a place/standing' vs H6965 'to rise'. With the prefix ב- and preceded by כל, 'in every place' (H4725) is the natural reading.
textual_notes: מ<ם contains a damaged character. Likely reads משם 'from there'.
The apostrophe character (') between תחפשו and הבתים indicates damaged or missing text. There may be a missing preposition or particle.
תחפשו could mean 'you shall search/seek out' or 'you shall disguise yourselves'. In context of going through houses preaching and healing, 'search through' is the more coherent reading.

verses.literal: And when you go out from there you shall search the houses seeking and healing the sick in every place

verses.translation: And Herod, the lord [or: ruler] [and] tetrarch, heard all the things that Yeshua had done, and he was in doubt [or: perplexity] on account of [the fact] that some were saying that Yochanan — he [is the one] who had returned alive.

translation_notes: אדון: H113 'sovereign/controller' vs H114 'Addon (name)'. Describing Herod's title alongside 'tetrarch', H113 'lord/ruler' is the coherent reading.
שמע: H8085 'to hear' vs H8086 (Aramaic 'to hear') vs H8087-8090 (names/nouns). As a verb ('Herod heard all the things'), H8085 is correct.
והיה: H1961 'to exist/be/become' vs H1962 'ruin' vs H3050 'Yah'. 'And it was to him in doubt' — H1961 is the clear verbal reading.

בספק: H5606 'to clap hands/chastisement' vs H5607 'chastisement; also satiety'. The word ספק in later Hebrew means 'doubt'. In context ('it was to him in doubt because people were saying...'), doubt/perplexity is the coherent image. Neither 'clapping' nor 'satiety' fits.
שיש: H7893 'marble' vs H3426 'there is/are'. The reading ש + יש = 'that there are (those saying)' produces the coherent clause. 'That marble saying' is nonsensical.
הוא: H1931 'he/it' as an emphatic pronoun. 'Yochanan — he [is the one] who returned alive.' Clear usage.
חי: H2416 'alive' vs H2417 (Aramaic 'alive'). Hebrew context, H2416.
textual_notes: בספק: The Strong's candidates (H5606/H5607) do not directly offer 'doubt', but ספק in post-biblical Hebrew means 'doubt/uncertainty'. This may reflect a later Hebrew stratum in the manuscript.
טטרקא is a transliteration of the Greek/Latin 'tetrarch' and has no Strong's entry.

verses.literal: And Herod lord tetrarch heard all the things that did Yeshua and it was to him in doubt on account of that there are [those] saying that Yochanan he [is] who returned alive

verses.translation: Others were saying, 'It is Eliyahu [Elijah], and he has appeared in the land.' And still others were saying that one of the ancient prophets — he [is the one] who has risen [back to] life.

translation_notes: אליהו: H453 is listed as 'Elihu', but the consonants אליהו equally support the prophet Elijah (אֵלִיָּהוּ). In context — speculation about who a miracle-worker might be — Elijah the prophet is the coherent identification, not Job's friend Elihu.
שאחד: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts' vs H259 'one/united/first'. After ש ('that'), 'that one of' (H259) produces the coherent clause.

מישישי: H3454 'Jeshishai, an Israelite'. However, the consonants can also be parsed as מ + ישישי = 'from the old/aged ones of', from ישיש (an aged person). Context ('one of the ancient prophets') demands the common noun reading, not a proper name.
הוא (both occurrences): H1931 emphatic pronoun 'he' — functioning as a copula in both clauses.
textual_notes: אליהו: The Strong's entry provided (H453) is for Elihu (Job's friend and other Israelites), but these same consonants represent the prophet Elijah. The context (speculation about prophetic figures returning) strongly points to Elijah.

מישישי: Could be parsed as the proper name Jeshishai (H3454) or as 'from the elders/ancient ones of'. The latter reading produces the coherent phrase 'one of the ancient prophets' and is clearly preferable.

verses.literal: Others saying Eliyahu he [is] and was seen in the land and others saying that one from [the] elders [of] the prophets he [is] who rose alive

verses.translation: And Herod said, 'I am the one who commanded to slaughter [or: behead] Yochanan. Who then is this one who does these things?' And he desired [or: was determined] to see Yeshua the Anointed One [Messiah].

translation_notes: ואמר: H559 'to say' vs H560 (Aramaic), H561-562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. As a verb opening reported speech ('And Herod said'), H559 is the clear choice.
אני: H589 'I' vs H590 'a ship/fleet'. Herod speaking about himself: 'I am the one who commanded' — H589.

לשחוט: The candidates listed under חוט are H2338 'to string together' and H2339 'a string/measuring tape'. However, the consonants לשחוט clearly represent the infinitive of שחט (H7819, 'to slaughter/kill'). The ש is part of the root, not a prefix. 'To slaughter Yochanan' is the only coherent reading.
זה: H2088 'this/that' vs H2089 'a sheep'. In the question 'who is he this?', H2088 demonstrative pronoun is correct.
אלו: H431 'lo!/these' vs H432 'if/nay'. Modifying דברים ('things'), 'these' (H431, functioning as a demonstrative) is the natural reading.
ורצה: H7521 'to be pleased with / to desire / to satisfy a debt'. 'He desired to see Yeshua' — the meaning 'desired/wished' fits perfectly.
משיח: H4899 'anointed/Messiah' vs H7878-7880 (ponder/shrub). As a title following Yeshua, 'Messiah/Anointed One' (H4899) is the clear reading.
textual_notes: לשחוט: The Strong's candidates provided (H2338/H2339 for חוט) do not match. The word is the infinitive of שחט 'to slaughter' (H7819), where the ש belongs to the root. This is unambiguous in context.
אלו as 'these' is post-biblical Hebrew usage. In biblical Hebrew, אלה would be expected. This suggests a later Hebrew stratum.
The placement of משיח ('Messiah') after ישוע could be the narrator's title for Yeshua rather than part of Herod's speech.

verses.literal: And said Herod I [am] he who commanded to slaughter Yochanan who is he this who does things these and he desired to see Yeshua Messiah

verses.translation: And the disciples returned to report [or: declare] to Yeshua the Anointed One [Messiah] all the things they had done. And Yeshua took them [aside] to a certain place called Beit Tzaidah [Bethsaida, House of Provision].

translation_notes: להגיד: The candidate H1517 (גיד = 'tendon') shares consonants but this is clearly the hiphil infinitive of נגד 'to tell/declare'. 'To declare to Yeshua all the things' is coherent; 'to tendon to Yeshua' is not.
שעשו: H6215 'Esav/Esau'. However, this is clearly the relative pronoun ש + the verb עשו (3mp perfect of עשה, 'they did'). 'All the things that they did' is the coherent reading, not 'that Esau'.
לקח: H3947 'to take' vs H3948 'instruction/something received'. As a verb with 'them' as object, 'took' (H3947) is correct.
במקום: H4725 'a place' vs H6965 'to rise'. With ב- prefix and followed by 'one called Beit Tzaidah', 'in a place' is the clear reading.
אחד: H258 'to unify' vs H259 'one/a certain'. Modifying מקום ('place'), 'one/a certain place' uses H259.
משיח: H4899 'Messiah/Anointed One' vs H7878-7880 (shrub/pondering). As a title following Yeshua, H4899 is unambiguous.
בית: H1004 'house' vs H1006 'Bajith' vs H3487 'object marker'. As the first element of a place name (Beit Tzaidah), H1004 'house' is correct.
צידה: H6720 'food/provision'. The place name Beit Tzaidah means 'House of Provision/Food' (= Bethsaida).
textual_notes: שעשו: The only Strong's candidate listed is H6215 (Esau), but the consonants are identical to the 3mp perfect of עשה 'to do/make'. Context decisively favors the verb.
צידה could also be related to ציד 'hunting/fishing', which would give 'House of Fishing' — an equally attested etymology for Bethsaida.

verses.literal: And returned the disciples to declare to Yeshua Messiah all the things that they did and Yeshua took them to [a] place one called Beit Tzaidah

verses.translation: And [when] that matter [or: word] became known [to] the peoples, they went after Yeshua, and he received them and spoke with them concerning the kingdom of YHWH, and [was] healing the sick. They would be — they would be clothed — their garments — you shall stand [firm] — that they would not receive — that they would receive — that [they do] not receive from that city — dust you shall shake off [or: desire].

translation_notes: והדבר (דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture', H1907 'vizier'. With the article ה and demonstrative ההוא following, this is a noun — 'the matter/word that.' Chose H1697.
ההוא (הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/that', H1932 same Aramaic, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. With the article prefix ה, this is the demonstrative 'that.' Chose H1931.

כאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. With prefix כ, כאשר = 'as/when' — standard relative conjunction. Chose H834.

ומדבר (דבר/מדבר): Candidates: H4057 'desert/speech', H1696 'to speak'. In context 'and-speaking with-them about the kingdom,' the participle form of H1696 (speaking) fits perfectly. H4057 'desert' would be incoherent here. Chose H1696 as participial form.

ומרפא (רפא): Candidates: H4832 'curative/medicine', H7495 'to cure/heal', H7496 'ghost', H7497 'giant'. In context of healing the sick, the participial form of H7495 'healing' is the natural reading. Chose H7495.
עיר: Candidates: H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young ass'. In context of receiving/not receiving from a place, 'city' is the coherent reading. Chose H5892.

עפר: Candidates: H6080 'to be dust', H6081 'Epher (name)', H6082 'a fawn', H6083 'dust'. In the context of shaking off from a city, 'dust' produces the clearest image — shaking dust off one's feet. Chose H6083.
לבוש: Candidates: H3830 'garment', H3831 same, H954 'to be ashamed'. In context alongside לבושים (garments), clothing is the coherent reading. Chose H3830.
textual_notes: This section appears to be a composite or fragmentary passage — multiple phrases seem to be variant readings or editorial notes stacked together (שלאיקבלו / שיקבלו / שלא יקבלו appear to be three attempts at the same phrase: 'that they do not receive'). The words יהיה / יהיו / לבוש ם / לבושים / תעמדו similarly seem like marginal variants or scribal alternatives rather than continuous prose.

תחפצו could be from חפץ H2654 'to delight/desire' or potentially a form meaning 'to shake off.' The context of dust from a city suggests a shaking-off gesture, but the consonants most naturally map to חפץ 'desire.' This remains genuinely ambiguous.
ידעשהו appears to be a compound: ידע (to know) + שהו (that-him/it), possibly 'knew it' or 'made it known.' No Strong's entry was provided; parsed as ידע (H3045) + pronominal suffix.

verses.translation: And [as] the day began to decline [or: descend], the twelve emissaries [or: sent-ones] approached him and said to him, 'Let this people go to their villages [or: fortified towns] and to their cities nearby to this place, so that they may be able to find something [to] eat, because this place is desolate [or: barren].'

translation_notes: עשר: Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6236 'ten (Aramaic)', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth', H6240 'teen (in combination)'. With ה<נים preceding (likely שנים = two), this forms 'twelve' — שנים עשר. Chose H6240 for the combinatory '-teen' sense, though H6235 also works.
זה (first): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Following העם, 'this people' is the coherent reading. H2089 'sheep' would be bizarre after 'the people.' Chose H2088.
למקום: Candidates: H4725 'a place/standing', H6965 'to rise'. With prefix ל and following demonstrative זה, 'to [this] place' is clear. Chose H4725.
הזה: Candidates: H1957 'to dream', H2088 'this'. Following המקום, 'this place' is the standard demonstrative construction. 'To dream' makes no sense here. Chose H2088.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 same Aramaic, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Functions as copula: 'it [is] desolate.' Chose H1931.

חרב: Candidates: H2717 'to parch/desolate', H2718 'to demolish', H2719 'sword', H2720 'parched/ruined', H2721 'drought/desolation', H2722 'Horeb'. As predicate adjective after הוא, H2720 'desolate/ruined' fits perfectly — describing a barren place with no food. Chose H2720.
textual_notes: ה<נים — the text has a damaged/unclear character marked with <. In context of 'the ___ ten emissaries,' this is almost certainly שנים (two), yielding 'the twelve emissaries.' The damaged letter is likely ש.
<יאכלו — also has a damaged character. Most likely שיאכלו ('that they will eat') or simply יאכלו ('they will eat'). The ש prefix would be the relative 'that.'
למגדליהם — could be from מגדל (H4026) 'tower' but in later Hebrew usage מגדל could refer to a village/hamlet. The pairing with 'their cities' suggests smaller settlements.

verses.translation: And Yeshua said to them, 'You give them [something] to eat.' And they said to him, 'We have nothing except [or: only] five loaves [of bread] and two fish, and we would need to buy food for all this people.'

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same Aramaic, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. As a verb preceding direct speech, H559 'said' is the clear choice. Chose H559.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'them'. As preposition ל + pronoun הם = 'to them,' this is standard. Chose H1992.
אין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/not', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. In context 'there is not to us except,' H369 is the natural negative existential. Chose H369.
לבד: Candidates from בד: H905 'separation/alone', H906 'linen', H907 'a lie'. With prefix ל, לבד = 'alone/only/except' — standard usage. Chose H905.
ושני: Candidates: H2059 'Vashni (name)', H8145 'second/two', H5204 'lamentation'. Before דגים (fish), 'two' is the only coherent reading. Chose H8145.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Before מאכל (food), 'thing of food' = something to eat. Chose H1697.
מאכל: Candidates: H3978 'food/eatable', H398 'to eat', H400 'food'. As a noun following דבר, H3978 'food' is the direct reading. Chose H3978.
הזה: Candidates: H1957 'to dream', H2088 'this'. After העם, 'this people' is standard. Chose H2088.
textual_notes: חמ<ה — damaged character. In context before לחמים (loaves) and with ושני דגים (and two fish), this is almost certainly חמשה (five), matching the well-known narrative of five loaves and two fish.

verses.translation: And they were about five thousand. And Yeshua said to his disciples, 'Make the people sit [in groups of] fifties by fifties.'

translation_notes: והם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. As subject pronoun opening a clause about quantity, 'they' is the only coherent reading. Chose H1992.
כמו: H3644 'as/about/thus'. Before a number (five thousand), 'about' fits perfectly — an approximation. Chose H3644.

עשו: Candidate listed: H6215 'Esau'. However, in context 'Yeshua said to his disciples _____ that they sit,' this must be the imperative plural of עשה (H6213) 'do/make.' The consonants עשו can be the imperative of עשה. The listing of H6215 'Esau' is clearly wrong for this context. Chose H6213.
העם: Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with'. As direct object of 'make sit,' 'the people' is correct. Chose H5971.
textual_notes: חמ<ים and לחמ<ים — both have damaged characters. Given the context of organizing groups, these are almost certainly חמשים (fifties). The ל prefix on the second instance creates a distributive: 'fifties by fifties' = in groups of fifty.
עשו — the only Strong's candidate provided is H6215 'Esau,' but the context absolutely demands the imperative of עשה (H6213) 'to do/make.' The consonants are identical.

verses.translation: And so they did.

translation_notes: כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. With prefix ו and followed by עשו (they did), 'and so' is the natural reading. Chose H3651.
עשו: Candidate listed: H6215 'Esau'. As in section 4, this is clearly the 3rd person plural perfect of עשה (H6213) 'to do.' 'And so they did' is coherent; 'and so Esau' is not. Chose H6213.

verses.translation: And Yeshua took the five loaves and the two fish, and looked up to the heavens [or: sky], and blessed them — the loaves and the two fish — and broke the bread and distributed [it] to his disciples, and commanded them to set it before that people.

This appears to be a Hebrew translator's rendering of the concept of a cross/execution stake using the imagery of crossed beams. The bracket around יקח suggests a scribal insertion or restoration.

The syntax is challenging: 'those who despise me and my words' could be the object of יבזם (the Son of the Father will despise them) or could be a separate clause. The reading where בן האב is the subject of יבזם is more coherent.

טוב: Candidates: H2895 'to be good', H2896 'good (adj.)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness (noun)'. Chose H2896 because it serves as an adjective modifying דבר.

textual_notes: אהלים: The Strong's candidate provided (H174 'aloe wood') does not match the context. The consonants equally spell the plural of אהל (H168 'tent'). I read it as 'tents/shelters'.

חי: Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 'alive (Aramaic)'. Chose H2416 as the predicate 'alive' describing the son after rising.

עד: Candidates: H5703 'perpetuity', H5704 'until', H5707 'witness'. Chose H5704 because 'until it distresses him' is temporal.
textual_notes: ורוק: Could be the verb H7324 'to pour out' or the noun 'spittle/saliva'. Both produce a coherent image. I read it as the noun since יוצא ('going out') already serves as the verb of the clause.
ומיד: Literally 'and from hand' but idiomatically 'immediately'. Could theoretically mean 'and from [his] hand' but 'immediately he cries out' is far more natural.

verses.literal: And the spirit seizes him and immediately [he] cries out and [it] shatters him and spit goes out from his mouth and it does not depart from him until it distresses him with force

textual_notes: רעה: While H7465 'breakage/evil' fits best, the consonants could also theoretically be read as a feminine adjective from רע (H7451 'bad/evil'), which is not listed among the candidates but shares the semantic field. Either way the meaning is 'evil/wicked'.

הזמן: Candidates: H2163 'to fix a time', H2164 'to agree', H2165 'an appointed occasion/time', H2166 'occasion (Aramaic)'. Chose H2165 because 'the time' (with article ה) is a noun.
נא: Candidates: H4994 'now/please/I pray', H4995 'raw/uncooked', H4996 'No (Thebes)'. Chose H4994 because 'bring now your son' is a command with an urgency particle.

translation_notes: המה: Candidates: H1993 'to make a loud sound/be in commotion', H1992 (from הם) 'they (emphatic)'. In context 'they saw thus were astonished' — the pronoun 'they' resuming the subject of 'the ones walking after him' is the natural reading.

verses.literal: Set your-hearts [to] these the-words the-destined to-come [the] son-of the-man will-be handed-over into-hands-of man

verses.translation: And they did not understand the word of YHWH [or: the LORD], for it was hidden [or: concealed] from them, and they feared [or: were afraid] to ask about it.

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction because/for/that'. As a conjunction introducing the reason they didn't understand, H3588 is clearly correct.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1992 (from הם) 'them'. As prepositional ל + pronoun הם = 'to/from them,' the pronominal reading is correct.

לשאול: Candidates: H7585 'Sheol/world of the dead', H7586 'Shaul (proper name)', H193 'body/powerful'. However, the root שאל 'to ask/inquire' is the standard verb here. With the infinitive ל prefix and the context 'they feared to _____ it,' 'to ask' is the only coherent reading. The candidates listed appear to be for שאול rather than the verb שאל, but the consonants לשאול clearly represent the infinitive of שאל.
textual_notes: The text appears fragmented: 'וי ר או' seems to be a broken form. Reading these three fragments together as וייראו (and they feared) makes contextual sense — 'they feared to ask about it.' The spacing may reflect manuscript damage or scribal convention. This is my reconstruction.

יהוה here is striking — the text says 'the word of YHWH' rather than what one might expect. This could indicate the speaker equates the utterance with divine speech, or מלת יהוה could be a scribal convention. I translate as found.

לשאול: The candidates given do not include the verb שאל 'to ask,' but the consonantal form לשאול is the standard infinitive construct of שאל with ל prefix. The candidates H7585/H7586 share consonants but produce nonsense in context ('they feared toward Sheol her').

verses.literal: And-not they-understood [the] word-of YHWH for it-was-hidden from-them and-they-feared to-ask it

verses.translation: And they debated [literally: carried and gave, i.e. argued back and forth] among themselves [about] who among them [was] greatest of all of them.

translation_notes: מהם: From הם H1992 'them' with preposition מ 'from' — 'from among them.' The other candidates (H1990 'Ham region', H1991 'abundance') produce incoherent readings.
textual_notes: ונשאו ונתנו is a Hebrew idiom meaning 'they debated/discussed' (literally 'they lifted and gave' i.e. exchanged words back and forth). This is a well-known Rabbinic Hebrew expression.

verses.literal: And-they-carried and-they-gave among-them who from-them [is] great from-all-of-them

translation_notes: לקח: Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction/something received'. As a verb with נער אחד as object, 'took' (H3947) is the clear reading.

נער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Following the verb 'took' and modified by 'one,' 'a boy/child' (H5288) produces the only coherent image.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/united'. As a numeral modifying נער, 'one' (H259) is the correct reading.

verses.literal: And-Yeshua as-knowing their-thoughts took [a] boy one and-brought-him-near to-him

translation_notes: ואמר: H559 'to say' — verb with Yeshua as implied subject and להם as indirect object.
להם: H1992 (הם 'them') with preposition ל — 'to them.' H3859 'to rankle' makes no sense here.

המקבל: Candidates: H6901 'to admit/take/receive', H6902 'to acquire', H6903 'in front of', H6904 'battering-ram', H6905 'presence'. The participle with article ה 'the one receiving' (H6901) is the only reading that fits the sentence structure.
נער: H5288 'a boy/child' — same reasoning as section 5.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Demonstrative 'this' modifying נער is the natural reading. H2089 'a sheep' would produce 'boy sheep' — incoherent.
בשמי: The candidates list H8060 'Shammai' and H4310 'who'. But בשמי is naturally ב + שם + י = 'in my name' (שם H8034 with 1cs pronominal suffix). The candidates seem incomplete.

והקטן: Candidates: H6994 'to diminish', H6995 'little finger', H6996 'small/diminutive', H6997 'Katan (name)'. With article ה and in context of comparing rank, 'the small/least one' (H6996) is correct.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. As a pronoun in a nominal clause 'he [is] great,' H1931 is the standard reading.
textual_notes: ש<לחני appears to have a scribal mark or damage indicated by <. The root שלח 'to send' (H7971) with 1cs suffix ני = 'sent me' is the clear reading. The < may indicate a letter that was damaged or uncertain in the manuscript.

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say' — Yochanan as subject, introducing direct speech.
אדם: Candidates: H119-H124. 'A man/human being' (H120) is the only coherent reading — they saw a person casting out demons.
אחד: H259 'one' — used as an indefinite article 'a certain [man].'

בידו: The candidate H3035 'Jiddo (proper name)' is irrelevant. This is ב + יד + ו = 'by his hand / against him.' In context of rebuking, it means 'we protested against him.'
כאשר: Candidates for אשר: H833-H838. With כ prefix, כאשר = 'as/when/because' — H834 'who/which/that/because' is the correct base. 'Because he is not walking after you with us.'
textual_notes: ה<דים has a scribal mark or damage (<). The expected word is השדים 'the demons' (from שד). The < likely represents a damaged or uncertain letter.
ומחינו could derive from מחה 'to protest/object' or מחא 'to strike/clap.' In context of rebuking someone, 'we protested/objected' fits best. The suffix נו = 'we.'
בידו could mean 'by his hand' (i.e., we physically stopped him) or be an idiom for 'against him.' Both readings are plausible; I chose the idiomatic sense of opposing him.

translation_notes: אמר: H559 'to say' — Yeshua as subject.

work: ואמר (א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the waw-consecutive + verbal form 'and he said' is the natural narrative reading.

מאי (מ + א-י): Candidates for אי: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because מ + אי = 'from where/what,' forming the interrogative 'from what' with זה following.

האדם (א-ד-ם): Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'human being/mankind', H121 'Adam (name)', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'son of the human' as a title is coherent, and the definite article ה points to the species/generic sense.
לא (ל-א): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808 because this is standard Hebrew negation.

לאבד (א-ב-ד): Candidates: H6 'to perish/destroy', H7 'to perish (Aramaic)', H8 'destruction'. Chose H6 because the infinitive construct with ל = 'to destroy' fits the causative/hiphil sense of the verb.
אלא: The only candidate H414 is 'Ela (a name)'. However, אלא in post-biblical Hebrew functions as an adversative conjunction 'but/rather/except.' Context demands the conjunction reading here.

אחר (א-ח-ר): Candidates: H309 'to delay', H310 'after/behind', H311 'after (Aramaic)', H312 'another/other', H313 'Acher (name)'. Chose H312 because 'another tower/village' describes their destination.
ambiguities: מ<ם contains a damaged character; likely משם ('from there') based on context of departing from a location.

אלא is not well attested in Biblical Hebrew Strong's (H414 is a proper name). This is a Mishnaic/post-biblical Hebrew conjunction meaning 'but rather,' suggesting the manuscript's Hebrew register includes post-biblical elements.

במגדול could be the Egyptian place name Migdol (H4024) or a common noun meaning 'tower/fortified village' (from מגדל H4026). הנח: Same as section 7 — Hiphil imperative 'leave/allow'. Not H5146 'Noah'.

The phrase 'leave the Ishmaelites to bury' is syntactically incomplete — 'to bury [whom/what]' is implied but not stated. The understood object is likely 'their dead' or 'your father' from the preceding verse.

translation_notes: ואדם (consonants א-ד-ם): H120 'human being/man' — a person speaking in narrative.

אמר (consonants א-מ-ר): H559 'to say' — speech verb.
אדון (consonants א-ד-ו-ן): H113 'sovereign/lord' — form of address.

אלך: H479 'these' is given, but contextually this is clearly 1cs imperfect of הלך 'I will go/walk'. The Strong's candidate does not match the verbal use.

verses.translation: And Yeshua said to him: The man who sets [or: places] his hand on the plow and looks back behind him is not worthy [or: fit] for the kingdom of YHWH.

translation_notes: וישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua', H3443 'Jeshua'. Proper name, H3442.
אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560-H564 (other readings). Introducing speech, H559.

ומביט — hiphil participle of נבט (to look/gaze), with waw: 'and looking.' Standard form.
אחריו — 'behind him,' from אחר (behind/after) with 3ms suffix.
אינו — negative existential אין with 3ms suffix: 'he is not.'
ראוי — 'fit/worthy/suitable.' This is a post-biblical Hebrew adjective. No Strong's number applies directly.

[] — empty brackets at the end suggest a lacuna or missing text in the manuscript. The sentence appears grammatically complete without it, though something may have followed (e.g., a qualifying phrase about the kingdom).

במלכות יהוה — the preposition ב could mean 'in' or 'for.' Both readings are viable: 'is not worthy in the kingdom of YHWH' or 'is not fit for the kingdom of YHWH.' The latter is more natural in English.

verses.literal: And Yeshua said to him the man the placing his hand on the plow and looking behind him is not fit in [the] kingdom [of] YHWH
